name: Five Star Program
summary: Annual grants for community partnerships in the United States that combine on-the-ground habitat restoration, such as wetland, riparian, coastal or urban tree canopy work, with local outreach, education and stewardship.
reporting: Grantees report on project metrics they choose from the programme's list in NFWF's Easygrants system, such as acres restored, trees planted and people reached.

eligibility.rule: A 501(c) nonprofit, state, local or municipal government, Tribal entity or educational institution
Not an unincorporated individual, business, international organization or U.S. federal agency
Project is within or adjacent to a geographic priority location
Provide a direct ecological benefit through at least one listed on-the-ground activity
Integrate meaningful outreach, education and/or training into the on-the-ground activities
Do not use funds for ongoing legal compliance, including permit conditions, mitigation or settlement agreements

co_finance.applies_to: All projects except NRCS People's Garden urban agriculture projects

documents: Statement of Litigation, unless a government applicant
Board of Trustees or Directors list, or statement that none exists
GAAP Audited Financial Statements, if requested in Easygrants
IRS Form 990, if requested in Easygrants
Single Audit, if requested in Easygrants

applicant_types.quote: Eligible applicants include non-profit 501(c) organizations, state government agencies, local governments, municipal governments, Tribal Governments and Organizations and educational institutions

geography.quote: providing measurable and meaningful conservation and educational outcomes in communities across the United States

access.quote: All application materials must be submitted online through National Fish and Wildlife Foundation's Easygrants system.

window.quote: NFWF anticipates one round of full proposals annually for this program.

amount.quote: Awards range from $30,000 to $150,000 with 30-40 grants awarded per year.

consortium_required.quote: Must involve five or more partners (public and/or private entities) including the applicant

reporting.quote: the Five Star program has a list of metrics in Easygrants for full proposal applicants to choose from for future reporting

effort.quote: Full Proposal Due Date June 4, 2026, by 11:59 PM EST

eligibility.quote: Eligible applicants include non-profit 501(c) organizations, state government agencies, local governments, municipal governments, Tribal Governments and Organizations and educational institutions
Ineligible applicants include unincorporated individuals, businesses, international organizations and U.S. Federal government agencies
Projects must be within or adjacent to these locations
all projects must provide a direct ecological benefit through one or more of the following
all projects must integrate meaningful outreach, education and/or training into the proposed on-the-ground activities through one or more of the following
NFWF funds may not be used to support ongoing efforts to comply with legal requirements, including permit conditions, mitigation and settlement agreements

co_finance.quote: Projects must have a minimum match of 1:0.75 non-federal cash or in-kind contributions. Larger match ratios and matching fund contributions from a diversity of partners are encouraged and will be more competitive. Projects applying for urban agriculture funding through the NRCS People's Garden Initiative do not require match.
